transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

Lately I keep thinking everyone would be better off without me, and I find myself planning how I might just not be here anymore. A friend from the community center got really worried about me and helped me come here today.
Have you ever had a similar episode of depression or suicidal thoughts before, or is this the first time this has happened?

No, this is the first time I've ever felt this way. These heavy, low feelings and thoughts of disappearing have been coming and going for about seven months now, ever since things got worse after my mother fell ill two years ago. Before all of this started, I never experienced these kinds of mood swings or thoughts.
Have these low mood and suicidal thoughts been present most of the time for the past seven months, or do they mainly happen only when you are dealing with the stress about your mother?

These heavy, low periods and thoughts of disappearing have been coming and going on and off for about seven months in total. Even though the worry about my mother is always there, these low stretches feel like they have a mind of their own and don't just happen when I'm dealing with her immediate stress.

During these past seven months, have you had any stretches of at least two weeks where you felt depressed or lost interest in things nearly every day, even when the stress about your mother was not the main thing on your mind?

Yes, there have been weeks at a time where a heavy, dark cloud just sits on my chest and I can't shake it. During those times, I completely lose interest in taking photos or going to the mosque, even when I'm not actively thinking about my mother's health. I just stay in my room staring at the wall because nothing feels worth the effort anymore.
Have you had this low mood and loss of interest for most of the day nearly every day for at least two weeks at a time, or does it usually improve when the stress about your mother eases?

Yes, those heavy feelings and losing interest in everything definitely last for weeks at a time, and it has been happening on and off for about seven months. It doesn't get better when the stress about my mother eases up; these feelings just keep affecting me on and off, and I haven't been able to go back to how I was before.

When these low periods happen, do they start within a few months of a specific stressful event or get clearly worse because of that stress, or do they seem to come on even when the stress is not changing?

This all started about two and a half years ago when my mother first fell very ill, which was a huge stress for me. But even though the worry about her is always there in the background, these low periods now seem to come and go on their own. They can hit me hard even when there hasn't been any new or sudden change in the stress.
Have your low mood and loss of interest mostly improved when the stress about your mother eases, or do they continue even during times when things feel a bit calmer?

I'm not really sure, it feels like the low mood just comes and goes on its own, even when things with my mother are a bit quieter. It doesn't seem to improve just because her situation is stable for a while.
Have these symptoms been present continuously for most of the past two years, or do they come and go for shorter periods after stress changes?

These mood swings and strange experiences have been affecting me on and off for a little over two years now, ever since my mother first got sick back home. During this whole time, I haven't really been able to go back to how I was before.
Have you had these low mood and loss of interest symptoms continuously for most of the past two years, or do they mainly come in response to stress and then ease up when the stress improves?

No, the low mood and loss of interest haven't been continuous for the whole two years. These heavy, low periods have been coming and going on and off, totaling about seven months in all. However, I still haven't really felt like my normal self since my mother first became ill over two years ago.
Have your low mood and loss of interest been present nearly every day for most of the past two weeks, or do they mainly come and go in response to stress and then improve when things are calmer?

Yes, during those low phases, the heavy, sinking feeling and complete lack of interest are there almost every day. It doesn't improve or go away when things are calm; I just feel flat and heavy, and I stay in my room staring at the wall regardless. These low periods have been coming and going like that for about seven months in total.
Have you had any changes in sleep, appetite, energy, concentration, or feelings of guilt or worthlessness during these low periods?

During these low periods, I have a heavy, sinking feeling in my chest that drains my energy and makes everything feel completely pointless. I also carry a lot of guilt, believing my mother's illness is my punishment for leaving India and that I am a useless, terrible son. My appetite drops completely during these times, to the point where I hardly touch my food and have lost several kilos.
During these low periods, have you ever heard or seen things that other people do not, or felt that someone was trying to harm you or that your thoughts were being controlled?

Yes, when I am alone at night, I hear a deep male voice that isn't mine telling me I'm a failure and that I should just go. I also get so scared because I feel like my coworkers and relatives in India are constantly watching my every move, sending secret messages about me through WhatsApp and even on the TV.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when the depression was gone, but you still heard voices or felt watched or controlled?

Yes, there was a stretch a few months ago when my mood felt more normal, not especially high or low. But even during those weeks, I was still sure people at work and back home were coordinating against me, and I kept hearing that man's voice at night.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when your mood was normal or only mildly low, but you still heard the voice or felt that people were watching or targeting you?

Yes, there was a stretch a few months ago when my mood felt completely normal, neither high nor low. But even during those weeks, I still heard that deep voice at night and was convinced that the people at work and back home were coordinating against me.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when your mood was completely normal or only mildly low, but the voices or beliefs that people were watching or targeting you were still present?

Yes, that's correct. A few months ago, my mood felt completely normal for a few weeks, neither high nor low. But even during that time, I still heard that deep voice at night and remained convinced that people at work and back in India were coordinating and sending messages about me.
Have you ever had a period of at least two weeks when your mood was completely normal or only mildly low, but the voices or beliefs that people were watching or targeting you were still present?

Yes, that definitely happened for a few weeks a few months ago when my mood felt relatively normal, neither high nor low. Even though I felt okay, I still heard that deep male voice at night and felt completely convinced that people at work and back home were coordinating against me.
Have you ever had any periods of at least 2 weeks when your mood was normal or only mildly low, but the voices or beliefs that people were watching or targeting you were still present?

Yes, that is exactly what happened for about two weeks a few months ago. My mood felt quite stable and normal, neither high nor low, but I still heard that deep voice at night. I also remained completely convinced that my coworkers and family were coordinating against me.
Have you ever had any periods of at least 2 weeks when your mood was normal or only mildly low, but the voices or beliefs that people were watching or targeting you were still present?

Yes, absolutely. A few months ago, I had a stretch of about two weeks where my mood felt completely normal, neither high nor low. But even during those weeks, I still heard that deep voice at night and felt sure that people were watching and coordinating against me.

Have you ever had a period of at least a week where you felt unusually energized or irritable, needed much less sleep, talked more than usual, had racing thoughts, or did risky things that were out of character?

Yes, I get these wired, "up" periods that have been coming and going for about the last year and eight months, often lasting for weeks at a time. During these phases, I feel unusually energized and irritable, sleeping only two or three hours a night without feeling tired while my thoughts race. I end up starting a hundred projects at once, like cleaning the apartment at 3 a.m. or making late-night calls to relatives in India because I just can't sit still.
During those energized or irritable periods, do they last at least 1 week and cause major problems at work, home, or with other people?

Yes, those wired periods definitely last for at least a week or more, and they have caused major problems for me. I am currently on a final warning at work because my performance has suffered so much, and at home, I let chores and bills pile up completely. I've also stopped going to the mosque and community center because of how chaotic everything gets.
Have the voices, paranoia, or feeling that people are watching you ever continued for at least 2 weeks when you were not having any depression or manic symptoms at all?

Yes, a few months ago there was a stretch of about two weeks where my mood felt completely normal, not too high, low, or excited. But even during that time, I still heard that deep voice at night and felt sure everyone was coordinating against me.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had no hallucinations, paranoia, or other psychotic symptoms at all, even if your mood was still high or low?

I'm not really sure, but it feels like those voices and the feelings of being watched are almost always there whenever my mood is acting up. I can't recall a clear two-week stretch where they completely went away while I was feeling very high or low.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you had no hallucinations, paranoia, or other psychotic symptoms at all, even if your mood was still high or low?

I'm really not sure about that. I can't recall ever having a period where my mood was very high or low but I didn't experience the voices or the feeling of being watched. They always seem to happen at the same time when my mood is off.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were clearly depressed or clearly manic, but you did not have any voices, paranoia, or other psychotic symptoms at all?

I don't think so, to be honest. It seems like the voices and the feeling of being watched are almost always there or get much worse whenever my mood swings. I really can't recall a clear two-week period where I had only the mood changes without any of those other experiences.
Have you ever had a period of at least 2 weeks when you were clearly depressed or clearly manic, but you did not have any voices, paranoia, or other psychotic symptoms at all?

I really don't think so. It feels like the voices and the feeling of being watched are almost always there or mixed in whenever my mood goes up or down. I can't recall a clear two-week period where I had only the mood changes without any of those strange experiences.
Have you ever had a clear period of at least 2 weeks when your mood was depressed or manic, but you had no voices, paranoia, or other psychotic symptoms at all?

I am really not sure, and I can't recall a specific period of at least two weeks where I had the mood swings completely on their own. The highs and lows always seem to overlap or blur together with the voices and paranoid thoughts.

During your high or low mood episodes, do the voices or paranoid thoughts happen only while your mood is clearly changed, or have they ever continued for at least 2 weeks when your mood was completely normal?

They don't just happen during the mood swings; they have definitely continued even when my mood was normal. A few months ago, I had a stretch of about two weeks where my mood felt relatively normal, but I still heard that deep voice at night and felt sure people at work and back home were coordinating against me.
Have you ever had any period of at least 2 weeks when you had hallucinations or paranoia but no major depression or manic symptoms at all?

Yes, a few months ago I had a stretch of about two weeks where my mood felt relatively normal, neither high nor low. But even during that time, I still heard that deep voice at night and felt sure people at work and back home were coordinating against me.
Have you ever had a full 2 weeks or more when you had the voices or paranoia but no clear depression or manic symptoms at all?

Yes, a few months ago I had a stretch of about two weeks where my mood felt completely normal, not high or depressed at all. But even though my mood felt okay, I still heard that deep voice at night and felt certain that people at work and back home were coordinating against me.
Have you ever had any period of at least 2 weeks when you had no hallucinations, paranoia, or other psychotic symptoms at all, even if your mood was still high or low?

I am not really sure, and I can't recall a specific period of two weeks where those feelings and voices completely went away while my mood was high or low. They always seem to be lurking or getting worse during those times, so they are almost always there.
